question: Who is the Platform Foundations certification (formerly Salesforce Certified Associate) for?
options: Developers with two or more years of Apex coding experience
Architects preparing for the Technical Architect review board
Administrators who already hold the Platform Administrator credential
People with up to six months of Salesforce user experience
explanation: Platform Foundations, previously called Salesforce Certified Associate, is for people who may have up to six months of experience using Salesforce.
whyWrong: Platform Foundations is entry level and needs no coding experience.
That is an expert-level path; this exam is the entry point.
Platform Foundations sits before Platform Administrator, not after it.

question: What does the Customer 360 Platform mean?
options: A single marketing product for sending email campaigns to customer lists
Salesforce products working together to connect customer data across teams
A dashboard that shows a full-circle chart of each customer's open cases
A premium support plan that gives customers round-the-clock phone access to Salesforce
explanation: Customer 360 is Salesforce’s connected set of products that brings customer data together across the organization.
whyWrong: Customer 360 spans many products, not one marketing tool.
Customer 360 is a connected set of products, not a dashboard chart.
Customer 360 is not a support plan; it describes how Salesforce products share customer data.

question: Which object is a central part of Salesforce’s CRM data model?
options: Account
Dashboard
Report
Email Template
explanation: Account is a core object for companies or people a business works with.
whyWrong: A Dashboard displays data; it is not a core CRM object.
A Report displays data; it is not a core CRM object.
An Email Template stores message content; it is not a core CRM object.

question: What is a Salesforce record?
options: A saved chart that summarizes many rows from a source report
A setting that controls which objects a user may open or edit
One item stored in an object, such as a single Account
One piece of information on an item, such as a phone number
explanation: A record is one set of data in an object, like one Account.
whyWrong: That describes a dashboard component, not a record.
That describes a permission, not a record.
That describes a field. A record is the whole item.

question: Where can users view their tasks and calendar in Salesforce?
options: The Schema Builder canvas in Setup
The AppExchange listing for their org
The Home page and the activity components
The report folder shared with their manager
explanation: The Home page and Activity components can show tasks and calendar information.
whyWrong: Schema Builder shows objects and relationships, not a user's tasks.
AppExchange is a marketplace for apps; it does not show tasks or events.
A report folder stores reports; it is not where users see their tasks and calendar.

question: What is a Salesforce Dashboard?
options: A filtered table of records from one object on its tab
A page that shows several report charts and metrics together
A reusable message layout with merge fields for sending email
A single grouped report with subtotals for each sales owner
explanation: A Dashboard brings several report charts and metrics together in one view.
whyWrong: That describes a list view.
That describes an email template.
That describes a summary report; a dashboard combines components from several reports.

question: Which Salesforce feature lets users collaborate on records in real time?
options: Validation rules
Scheduled report subscriptions
Chatter and Activity
Duplicate rules
explanation: Chatter and Activity support record collaboration through comments, mentions, and related interactions.
whyWrong: Validation rules check data on save; they are not collaboration tools.
Report subscriptions email report results on a schedule; they are not real-time collaboration.
Duplicate rules stop or flag duplicate records; they do not support collaboration.

question: What is Lightning Experience?
options: Salesforce’s older user interface, kept for orgs that have not yet switched over
A programming interface that lets outside systems read and write records
A mobile-only app that replaces the desktop version of Salesforce
Salesforce’s modern user interface, with responsive design and newer features
explanation: Lightning Experience is Salesforce’s modern user interface, designed to work across screen sizes and offer current features.
whyWrong: That describes Salesforce Classic.
That describes an API, not a user interface.
Lightning Experience is the desktop interface; the Salesforce mobile app is separate.

question: A user wants to check whether Salesforce is having a service disruption right now. Where should they look?
options: IdeaExchange, the product ideas site
AppExchange, the apps marketplace
Trailhead, the free learning site
trust.salesforce.com, the status site
explanation: trust.salesforce.com shows real-time system status, incidents, and planned maintenance for each Salesforce instance.
whyWrong: IdeaExchange is where customers suggest and vote on product ideas; it does not report system status.
AppExchange lists apps and components to install; it does not report system status.
Trailhead teaches Salesforce skills; it does not report system status.

question: What is a Salesforce List View?
options: A table of records from one object, filtered by chosen conditions
A definition of which objects and fields a report is able to use
A bundle of permissions that can be assigned on top of a profile
A page of charts in which each component draws on one source report
explanation: A List View shows a filtered set of records in a table.
whyWrong: That describes a report type.
That describes a permission set.
That describes a dashboard.

question: Which navigation tools help users find apps and records in Salesforce?
options: Schema Builder and Data Loader
App Launcher and global search
Flow Builder and validation rules
Report Builder and dashboard filters
explanation: The App Launcher helps users open apps, and global search helps them find records and other content.
whyWrong: Schema Builder shows the data model and Data Loader moves data; neither is for everyday navigation.
These automate work and check data; they do not help users find apps or records.
These build and filter analytics; they are not the main way to find apps and records.

question: A sales rep wants to see open Opportunities as cards grouped by stage and drag a card to a new stage. What should they use?
options: A dashboard built on a source report
The Kanban view of a list view
A joined report with two blocks
The Favorites list in the header
explanation: The Kanban view displays a list view's records as cards in columns, and dragging a card to another column updates the record.
whyWrong: A dashboard displays report data as charts; records cannot be dragged between stages on it.
A joined report combines report blocks; it is read-only and has no cards to drag.
Favorites are shortcuts to pages and records a user visits often; they do not group records by stage.

question: A manager needs a report that groups Opportunities by owner and shows a subtotal for each owner. Which report format fits?
options: A tabular report, a plain list of rows
A list view pinned on the object tab
A summary report, grouped by rows
A report folder shared with the team
explanation: A summary report groups rows by a field such as owner and can show subtotals for each group. A matrix report is needed only when grouping by both rows and columns.
whyWrong: A tabular report lists rows without groupings, so it cannot show subtotals per owner.
A list view filters records on an object tab; it does not produce grouped subtotals.
A report folder stores and shares reports; it is not a report format.

question: What do Salesforce Reports do?
options: Organize, filter, and display data from Salesforce records
Send scheduled marketing emails to a list of selected contacts
Assign new records to users based on a set of routing criteria
Prevent records from saving when a field fails a set condition
explanation: Reports let users select, organize, filter, and display data from Salesforce records.
whyWrong: Sending email is not what a report does.
That describes assignment rules.
That describes a validation rule.

question: Which Salesforce record represents a potential sale?
options: Lead
Account
Campaign Member
Opportunity
explanation: An Opportunity represents a potential sale or deal the team is pursuing.
whyWrong: A Lead is a prospect who has not yet been qualified.
An Account represents a company or other organization.
A Campaign Member links a lead or contact to a campaign; it is not a sale.

question: What happens when a Lead gets converted?
options: It creates an Account and a Contact, and can also create an Opportunity
It deletes the Lead and its activity history without creating other records
It changes the Lead's status to Closed and keeps it as an open Lead record
It creates a Case and a Campaign so the service team can follow up
explanation: Converting a Lead turns it into an Account and a Contact, and optionally an Opportunity if there's a deal to track.
whyWrong: Conversion creates new records; it does not simply delete the Lead.
A status change alone is not a conversion; conversion creates new records.
A Case tracks a customer issue; it is not part of Lead conversion.

question: Which two things together control what a Salesforce user can do and see?
options: The role hierarchy alone, which sets both actions and record access
Profiles and permission sets for actions, plus record sharing for records
Login hours and password policies, which set what a signed-in user is able to do
Dashboards and report folders, which decide which data appears on screen
explanation: Profiles and permission sets decide what objects, fields, and actions a user has. Org-wide defaults, roles, and sharing rules separately decide which individual records they can reach.
whyWrong: The role hierarchy affects record access only, not what actions a user can take.
These control signing in, not what a user can do afterwards.
These display and organize analytics; they do not grant access to objects or records.

question: A team wants to stop records from saving unless a required field is filled in. What should they use?
options: A dashboard filter
A list view chart
A validation rule
A permission set
explanation: A validation rule checks a record against a condition and blocks the save with an error message if it fails.
whyWrong: A dashboard filter changes what a dashboard shows; it does not block a save.
A list view chart summarizes the records in a list; it has no effect on saving.
A permission set grants access, it doesn't check field values on save.

question: Before changing something in a live Salesforce org, a team wants to build and test it safely first. What should they use?
options: A dashboard
A report
A queue
A sandbox
explanation: A sandbox is a copy of the org used to build and test changes before moving them to production.
whyWrong: A dashboard just displays report data, it isn't an environment for testing changes.
A report organizes and displays records, it isn't a testing environment.
A queue holds records for a team to work from, it has nothing to do with testing changes.

question: A company wants to install a pre-built app into their Salesforce org instead of building it from scratch. Where would they look?
options: AppExchange
Trailhead
The Trailblazer Community
IdeaExchange
explanation: AppExchange is Salesforce's marketplace for installable apps and components, free and paid.
whyWrong: Trailhead is Salesforce's free learning site, it doesn't host installable apps.
The Trailblazer Community is a forum for questions and discussion, not an app marketplace.
IdeaExchange is where customers suggest and vote on product ideas, not where apps are installed from.
